Plugin.Details: Detects mismatched format strings in JBoss Logging calls (debugf/infof/warnf/errorf and debugv/infov/warnv/errorv family).

BugPattern.ShortDescription: Logging format string placeholder count does not match argument count
BugPattern.LongDescription:
The number of placeholders in the format string does not match the number of arguments supplied to the logging call.
If there are more placeholders than arguments, a MissingFormatArgumentException will be thrown at runtime (for printf-style *f methods) or the placeholder will be rendered literally (for MessageFormat-style *v methods).
If there are fewer placeholders than arguments, the extra arguments are silently discarded, which hides information that was intended to appear in the log output.
BugPattern.Details:
The number of placeholders in the format string does not match the number of arguments supplied to the logging call.

Too few placeholders (more args than placeholders): extra arguments are silently dropped — information is lost from the log entry.

Too many placeholders (fewer args than placeholders): a {@code MissingFormatArgumentException} is thrown at runtime for printf-style calls, or the placeholder is rendered literally for MessageFormat-style calls.

Example of broken code:

// Two %s placeholders but only one argument — will throw at runtime
logger.debugf("Loading realm %s from provider %s", realmName);

Corrected code:

logger.debugf("Loading realm %s from provider %s", realmName, providerName);

BugPattern.ShortDescription: Wrong placeholder syntax for the logging method variant used
BugPattern.LongDescription:
The format string uses the wrong placeholder syntax for the logging method called.
The *f family (debugf, infof, warnf, errorf, tracef, fatalf) uses printf-style placeholders: %s, %d, %f, etc.
The *v family (debugv, infov, warnv, errorv, tracev, fatalv) uses MessageFormat-style placeholders: {0}, {1}, {2}, etc.
Using %s in a *v call will cause the placeholder to appear literally in the output. Using {0} in a *f call will cause the placeholder to appear literally in the output.
BugPattern.Details:
The format string uses a placeholder syntax that does not match the logging method variant.

  • {@code *f} methods ({@code debugf}, {@code infof}, {@code warnf}, {@code errorf}, {@code tracef}, {@code fatalf}) use printf-style placeholders: {@code %s}, {@code %d}, …
  • {@code *v} methods ({@code debugv}, {@code infov}, {@code warnv}, {@code errorv}, {@code tracev}, {@code fatalv}) use MessageFormat-style placeholders: {@code {0}}, {@code {1}}, …

Example of broken code:

// debugv expects {0} style, but %s is used — placeholder appears literally
logger.debugv("Token expiry: %s", expiryTime);

Corrected code — either switch to the right method:

logger.debugf("Token expiry: %s", expiryTime);
// or switch to the right placeholder style:
logger.debugv("Token expiry: {0}", expiryTime);

Detector.Details: Detects mismatches between JBoss Logging format string placeholders and the number or style of arguments supplied. Covers the *f (printf-style) and *v (MessageFormat-style) method families on org.jboss.logging.Logger.
